meta.description: Section 4 jagged map: where AI stands against people, one row per domain, on the five steps of the s4 headings.
meta.source: already-past-us.md, section 4 (rows icpc and research-math from section 0, which section 4 places at the far right)

tiers.label: Ahead of trained or typical people

rows.comparison_text: Epoch AI's review found robots typically 3 to 10 times slower than people. No robot has yet been shown doing every part of cleaning a kitchen.

2025-11-07.comparison_text: Predecessor test: roboticist Benjie Holson's 'Humanoid Olympics' set 15 everyday tasks. A robot passed if it did a task on its own within 10 times as long as he took. By 16 October 2025 only one entry had passed: walking through a door with a round knob. A 2024 US government review of company videos also found robots slower than average people at simple tasks.
2025-11-07.ai_value: 1 of 15 everyday tasks passed so far (predecessor test)
2025-11-07.human_value: the organiser's own time on each task (robots allowed up to 10 times as long)

rows.comparison_text: People have solved every game. Every frontier model scored under 1% at launch in March 2026; by September GPT-6 Astra reached a verified 62.7% on ARC Prize's standard setup.

2025-11-07.comparison_text: The full ARC-AGI-3 test did not exist yet; only an early preview with a few games did. When ARC Prize tried two leading models, OpenAI's o3 and xAI's Grok 4, on the preview in July 2025, neither finished a single level. People could solve the games.
2025-11-07.ai_value: 0% (o3 and Grok 4 finished no levels; preview games)
2025-11-07.human_value: people beat the preview games (ARC Prize: "Humans: 100%")

2026-05-07.comparison_text: People have solved every game. By early May 2026 every leading AI model tested was still under 1%. GPT-5.5, the newest model ARC Prize had tested, scored 0.43% on its standard setup.

rows.comparison_text: On the Remote Labor Index, the best agent's work was judged as good as a human freelancer's on about 21% of 240 real paid projects.

2025-11-07.comparison_text: The Remote Labor Index had just launched (30 October 2025). The best agent, Manus, was judged as good as a human freelancer's work on 2.5% of 240 real paid projects.

2026-05-07.comparison_text: On the Remote Labor Index, the best agent was Claude Opus 4.6 running in Anthropic's Cowork app. Its work was judged as good as a human freelancer's on about 4% of 240 real paid projects.

rows.comparison_text: The Forecasting Research Institute found the best AI forecasters statistically indistinguishable from superforecasters on its questions. The superforecaster baseline was collected in 2024 and is extrapolated.

2025-11-07.comparison_text: On the Forecasting Research Institute's ForecastBench, superforecasters still beat the best AI (GPT-4.5), though FRI called the gap modest. AI already beat ordinary members of the public. The superforecaster baseline was collected in 2024 and is extrapolated.

2026-05-07.comparison_text: Superforecasters still led ForecastBench. The best AI systems, from Cassi and xAI, were about one year of AI progress behind, a gap FRI called substantial.
2026-05-07.ai_value: Brier 0.103 (Cassi ensemble and xAI Grok 4.20 Preview, tied; lower is better)

rows.tier_label: Level with the best, if confirmed
rows.comparison_text: Huawei, Xiaohongshu and others reported perfect scores of 42 out of 42. The IMO has confirmed none of them. 7 of the 666 human contestants also got full marks, so even if true it is a tie with the best.

2025-11-07.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
2025-11-07.comparison_text: At the 2025 olympiad, the one before IMO 2026, Google DeepMind's AI scored 35 out of 42. IMO graders marked it, and it was the lowest gold-medal score. That beat most of the 630 students, but 26 scored higher and 5 got full marks.
2025-11-07.human_value: 35/42 was the gold cutoff; 26 of 630 contestants scored higher, 5 got 42/42

2026-05-07.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
2026-05-07.comparison_text: IMO 2026 had not been held yet. The latest IMO result was still from 2025: Google DeepMind's AI scored 35 out of 42, marked by IMO graders. That was the lowest gold-medal score: 26 of the 630 students scored higher and 5 got full marks.
2026-05-07.human_value: 35/42 was the gold cutoff; 26 of 630 contestants scored higher, 5 got 42/42

rows.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
rows.comparison_text: Waymo says its driverless cars had 95% fewer serious-injury crashes than human drivers over 270 million miles. That is Waymo's own analysis, against average drivers in the same places.

2025-11-07.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
2025-11-07.comparison_text: Waymo said its driverless cars had 91% fewer serious-injury crashes than human drivers over 96 million miles through June 2025. That is Waymo's own analysis, against average drivers in the same places.

2026-05-07.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
2026-05-07.comparison_text: Waymo said its driverless cars had 92% fewer serious-injury crashes than human drivers over 170.7 million miles through December 2025. That is Waymo's own analysis, against average drivers in the same places.

rows.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
rows.comparison_text: In a randomised trial in Pakistan using written clinical cases, not real patients, GPT-4o alone scored 82.9%, doctors using GPT-4o 71.4% and doctors using ordinary references 42.6%. AI alone versus doctors with AI is an exploratory finding.
rows.human_value: 71.4% doctors with GPT-4o; 42.6% with ordinary references

2025-11-07.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
2025-11-07.comparison_text: In an earlier randomised trial in the US using six written clinical cases, not real patients, GPT-4 alone scored 92%, doctors using GPT-4 76% and doctors using ordinary references 74%. AI alone versus doctors is an exploratory finding, and this is a predecessor of today's Pakistan trial.
2025-11-07.human_value: 76% doctors with GPT-4; 74% with ordinary references

rows.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
rows.comparison_text: In Epoch AI's testing, Gemini 4 Argon scored 96% (October 2026). PhD experts scored about 70%, a baseline OpenAI measured. The questions are multiple-choice.

2025-11-07.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
2025-11-07.comparison_text: In Epoch AI's testing, Grok 4 scored 87% (July 2025). PhD experts scored about 70%, a baseline OpenAI measured. The questions are multiple-choice.

2026-05-07.tier_label: Ahead of trained or typical people
2026-05-07.comparison_text: In Epoch AI's testing, GPT-5.4 Pro scored 95% (March 2026). PhD experts scored about 70%, a baseline OpenAI measured. The questions are multiple-choice.

rows.comparison_text: According to press coverage of the US National Hurricane Center's review of the 2025 season, Google DeepMind's model did slightly better than the official Atlantic track forecasts at some lead times.
rows.ai_value: slightly better at some lead times

2025-11-07.tier_label: Beyond the best humans, if confirmed
2025-11-07.comparison_text: The 2025 hurricane season was still running. Early, unofficial checks by two independent hurricane experts found Google DeepMind's model had beaten the US National Hurricane Center's official track forecasts. No figures for that comparison were published, and the Center's own review was still months away.
2025-11-07.ai_value: beat the official track forecasts (preliminary, unofficial check)

rows.tier_label: Improving on the best known algorithms
rows.comparison_text: Google DeepMind's GenCast beat Europe's leading physics-based forecast ensemble on 97.2% of 1,320 test targets. That comparison is with another computer model, not with human forecasters.
An OpenAI model disproved Paul Erdős's 1946 unit distance conjecture. Nine mathematicians checked it. Humans improved on the AI's construction within weeks.

2025-11-07.comparison_text: This is an earlier, narrower kind of result. Google DeepMind says its AlphaEvolve system beat the best known answers on about 20% of more than 50 open math problems. For example, it multiplied 4x4 complex matrices with 48 multiplications, where the best known method of this kind, from 1969, used 49. It had slightly improved bounds on a few Erdős problems, but no AI had yet solved an open one.
2025-11-07.ai_value: beat the best known answer on about 1 in 5 of 50+ open problems

2026-05-07.comparison_text: OpenAI's GPT-5.4 Pro produced a proof of a 1966 conjecture by Erdős and two colleagues, listed as Erdős problem #1196. Mathematicians including Terence Tao checked it, made it shorter, and published it. Tao warned that failed AI attempts usually go unreported.

rows.comparison_text: On OpenAI's own account, its system solved all 12 problems at the 2025 world finals. The best human team solved 11. We found no ICPC statement on it.
